column1: - ATLAS maps adversary tactics and techniques against AI-enabled systems, AI capability abuse, and harmful autonomous behavior backed by case studies and red-team evidence · - Content release v2026.08 adds agentic techniques (AML.T0116 through AML.T0128) and renames AI Attack Staging to AI Attack Adaptation · - Monthly content releases (YYYY.MM) are separate from data format semver (6.0.0); manifest ties versions in GitHub atlas-data · - Platforms field on techniques tags Predictive AI, Generative AI, Agentic AI, and Enterprise scope
column2: - Living taxonomy: same technique ID may gain sub-techniques or maturity labels without changing the core attack story · - Navigator layers and STIX exports reflect the selected content version; diff releases rather than a single static PDF · - Case studies lag real-world agent deployments; technique maturity marks emerging vs validated entries
column3: - Map production AI controls and detections to ATLAS techniques and mitigations during threat modeling · - Subscribe to mitre-atlas/atlas-data releases and patch local Navigator layers when v2026.08 or later ships · - Use case studies as test scenarios for red teams; contribute new cases through ATLAS submission workflows · - Pair ATLAS agentic techniques with OWASP Agentic Top 10 and MCP-specific controls where tools and memory appear

column1: - European baseline for deployable AI systems using deep neural networks, including generative AI, across the full lifecycle · - Thirteen principles in five phases: secure design, development, deployment, maintenance, and end of life · - Addresses AI-specific risks: data poisoning, model obfuscation, indirect prompt injection, and training-data handling gaps · - Signposts ISO/IEC 22989 lifecycle stages, ETSI TR 104 128 implementation guide, and TS 104 216 conformance assessment
column2: - Out of scope for research-only AI never intended for deployment · - Does not replace ISO/IEC 27001; maps to existing cyber programs rather than duplicating generic IT controls · - Modal verbs follow ETSI drafting rules (shall/should/may); must/must not do not appear in deliverables
column3: - Assign lifecycle owners for each of the thirteen principles from design through model disposal · - Run asset identification and supply-chain tracking for data, models, prompts, and training infrastructure (Principles 5–8) · - Test and evaluate before release; monitor behavior in production; patch and mitigate on a cadence (Principles 9–12) · - Document end-user and affected-entity communications at deployment; dispose data and models at end of life (Principles 10, 13)

column1: - Frontier AI compresses discovery-to-exploitation windows; industry data cited puts weaponisation near 15 minutes and median exfiltration near 72 minutes after access · - Negative time-to-exploit: attackers may hold working exploits before vendor fixes ship, especially when patches reveal flaws in unsupported versions · - Defenders must treat environments as potentially compromised and extend ML-based prevention to agentic endpoints and enterprise browsers · - Security fundamentals stay central: asset inventory, patching discipline, segmentation, monitoring, and coordinated disclosure at machine speed
column2: - Position paper, not a binding regulation; recommendations will align to a future European Commission action plan · - Open-source maintainers and SMEs face report-volume spikes from AI-generated findings; triage capacity becomes the bottleneck · - Change-advisory workflows cannot approve fixes quickly enough when exploit windows are minutes; governance must allow faster intervention
column3: - Shift effort from discovery volume to risk-based prioritisation with faster triage and remediation · - Target single-digit-minute MTTD, MTTR, and MTTC where feasible; automate patching and containment paths · - Embed continuous threat modeling with AI-assisted simulation against live architectures · - Integrate defensive AI across SDLC and incident response with humans retained in approval loops · - Prepare CRA Single Reporting Platform workflows assuming active exploitation when awareness begins
